Twin stick rush shooter that is not too long, not too hard, and not too much bullet hell. To fully complete the game will take considerable effort but it's possible and satisfying to pick up and play the game, and with a bit of luck to complete the "base" run.


Luck plays a role in Rush Rover. There are some upgrades that make chances of success considerably higher, but alas drops are random and some times you feel like you get absolutely nothing all run.
Fortunately, skill is more important than luck. Getting through an arena without taking damage yields extra upgrade points which means you'll be stronger late in the run. Beating the time limit also gives a reward and for your best chances you want to finish every arena in time and without taking damage.

This is a very important feature. It made me think of Enter the Gungeon and how much i hated starting over because the first two levels were hella easy and boring, esp. after a losing a run on a much tougher level. Even skilled play made no difference. Rush Rover isn't frustrating when you have to restart.

What is frustrating is losing a run to a cheap death and there will be a few of those. Not all deaths are registered equal, and a few times i felt i lost not because i played badly but because the game just screwed me over.
Unfortunately this also includes a crash. The Blade Module is bugged and will crash the game. The only way to know is to try to use it. Or to read this.

The bug is a shame because this is a very polished and well behaved game otherwise, especially for a Game Maker game as those tend to be un-optimized and suffer from difficult to fix bugs. I've had a lot more trouble with the brilliant Risk of Rain.

Balance overall is pretty ok. Some weapons are a lot better than others but upgrading all systems depends of getting a lot of upgrade points, and being fully upgraded is more important than lucking into a "carry" weapon or plugin.

Ok, lets get the Nuclear Throne comparison out of the way. Throne is harder and more unforgiving, esp. in later levels when the random layout immediately drenches you in enemy gunfire. Throne is also more stylish and interesting. Gameplay wise they are similar with Rush Rover having more varied upgrades the player can use, but this is expected because there is only one character to play. It is also a lot more focused on boss fights.

The boss fights are a treat. They require some patience while you figure out the bullet hell attack patterns. Some of the bosses are absolutely cruel. They're almost impossible to beat without taking damage without a few upgrades such as the one that reduces your rover's hitbox size! or the ability to block or shield bullet spam.
That said, it's not required to beat bosses without damage. It helps though and there's achievements for that.

A very welcome feature is the ability to exit and save game anywhere, anytime, no questions asked. That's not common for the genre but i think it should be. It's just convenient and takes away none of the danger or difficulty.

I've given this game as much of a chance as I can, and despite loving both bullet hells and roguelites/roguelikes, I can't enjoy this game. There's several reasons for that. I'll be comparing this to monolith and enter the gungeon since both are roguelike bullet hells, and are direct competitors with this title.

For starters, Rush Rover starts slow. Like, [i]very slow[/i]. This creates a sense of dread when starting up another game. That sucks since you'll be dying quite a bit here. Why? It isn't always difficulty. This game prefers less brutal, reaction like difficulty, deadcells being an example. Rush Rover prefers a slow burn. That difficulty styling is precisely why the start is so slow. The enemies don't shoot much for the first 30 minutes, and because of that, you're guaranteed to get that far in every run. You won't be challenged much until then, outside of holding your interest.

Once thirty minutes have passed, you'll find yourself wailing on enemies for minutes at a time just to get through a single room. It takes an eternity. Rooms are large as well, and they take forever to navigate. Even if you manage to do so, you'll still struggle to chip enemies down over time. Instead, you end up being the one who gets chipped down, and that sucks. I want an exciting, action packed game when I play rogues, not  slow slog up to reasonable difficulty.

In my case, I've desperately struggled through difficult games before. It's standard fare for rogues, and anyone that's played deadcells, enter the gungeon, etc. knows this. This game is also hard, but it's not for the right reasons. It's because holding your attention on this game feels like discipline more than fun. Because of that and the lack of fun I had here, I can't reccommend this title.

全方位型のシューティングゲーム。

操作方法
左レバー　移動
右レバー　発射方向と射撃
YとX　メニューとマップ　メニューでパワーアップする
Ｌ２　ダッシュ
Ｒ１　特殊兵器
Ｒ２　武器の自動発射、普段はこれを押しっぱなしで、時々右レバーで方向を修正する使い方をする。
コンフィグでAimAssistをオンにする事で、プレイが楽になる。

メニューでのパワーアップ
真上　自機のウェポンの威力アップ、普段はこれを最優先で上げる。
左上　自機の移動速度　次に少し上げる
右上　ダッシュの能力
右　　一緒に付いてくるロボットの武器の威力
その他は、ゲーム中にアンロックする事で使えるようになる。

武器としては、発射間隔が短いものが良い。
ロケットランチャーは一見便利ですが、発射間隔が長い為に体当たりされる。
発射間隔が長い事は、それだけ攻撃力は低く、隙が大きいのでこのゲームでは不利になる。

最もお薦めはパルスガン、次に反射レーザー、
パルスガンはアドバンスにすると、敵弾を消せるので、生存力が極端に上がる。
サブウェポンとして、ショックウェーブが、これも敵弾を消せる上で超強力なのでお薦め。
オプションの武器は、近距離に高威力の武器だと接近戦に強い。FLUXRAYなど。
また、敵弾を遅くする、PulseForceも便利。

武器の威力を上げる事を重視して、包囲されないようにする事がお薦め。
その次に、自機の移動速度、オプションとサブウェポンの武器の威力を上げると、
包囲される前に倒し易くなり、生存力が増す。

Really impressive rogue-like, especially considering the lone ranger development style. The highlight by far is the weapons, items, and probes. There are tons, they're really distinctive and you get enough resources to really experiment around, especially once you get good enough to get the unscathed/time bonuses for clearing rooms. When you get a setup with a real good synergy it's suuuuper fun to be a wrecking ball in the battles which get huge and awesome, especially on hard mode.

The pacing is really great. Very little downtime running through empty rooms and lots of enemies with risk-free moments in between to level up and try new combos. Leveling up affects the slot, not the item in it so if you change to a new weapon/probe it transfers the upgrade, which encourages this games best part- experimenting with the awesome items. The blueprint system unlocks item creation so you can get to good combos faster once you know what you like.

Since one of the defining characteristic of a rogue-like is that nothing is explained in the game at all and you basically have to have the wikia up on your phone as you play, big credit to Rush for having descriptions and stats for all the weapons in the game.

Downsides are the aesthetics are a little monotone. Character design is great but the background is meh and never changes. Would have been nice to give the different areas a unique color at least. 

Highly recommended. Worth $20 and you can get it for $5.

Is Rush Rover innovative, fresh, or unique in any way? no.

What this game does is impressive. Dodging feels just incredible, I don't think I've played any other game where the bullet hell dodging felt so tight and well done. While we're on that, I want to mention the patterns in this game are also very well done. I never feel bullshitted out of a win, everything feels fair.

The item and upgrade system is mediocre. It gets the job done, and you can still have unique(ish) runs, but it's pretty run of the mill. I do appreciate the "core upgrading" system, where you gain XP to level up, and then use that to upgrade movement speed, your weapon, familiar, and a few other things. There isn't a whole lot here in that aspect, but it's passable to keep things entertaining.

Enemies are all the same boring color. orange this, orange that, very little variation here. It can get boring to look at this game. The areas all look kinda the same, except some have a little bit of grass, and some a little bit of snow. It's a visually "boring" game.

The level generation is interesting in some ways. It's room based like Isaac or Gungeon, but each room feels like a mini Nuclear Throne level. It's a bit of a new way of making these rooms, and it makes the game feel a little bit faster, and overall better. There's no specific shop rooms here, you find items in the rooms themselves, which gives you a good reason to scavenge the floor and not just rush to the finish. They do away with floors. The ENTIRE run is one massive floor, allowing for significant backtracking, makes the game almost feel open world-y, and makes the game's pacing a little bit faster.

I want to talk about a major point here, and that's the game's balancing. This is one of the few roguelikes where you can't outpace the game in power. Because of this, you can't just tear apart a room and not worry about getting hit. The game stays a challenge throughout the entire run, regardless of your items.

[I wouldn't call this a review. I'd call this an analyzation, or a discussion. I wanted to just talk about the game here and show my thoughts. Because of this, I will not be giving Rush Rover a numerical score.]
